text: To mitigate something bad is to make it smaller or less harsh. Some salt makers say their salt makes the harm from sodium smaller.
A deficiency is a shortage of something your body needs. Here it means not getting enough iodine.
Excessive means much more than is needed or healthy. A little salt is fine, but too much causes trouble.
Sodium is a mineral found in salt. Your body needs a little, but too much pushes blood pressure up.
Blood pressure is how hard your blood pushes on the walls of your blood vessels as your heart pumps.
Cardiovascular means having to do with the heart and the blood vessels that carry blood around the body.
To hydrate is to give a body or a thing the water it needs.
The bloodstream is the blood flowing around inside your body, carrying water and food to every part.
Here, contract means to get shorter and tighter. Muscles contract to move your body, then relax. It can also mean a written agreement, but not here.
The intestines are the long tubes in your belly where food is broken down and its nutrients are taken in.
To absorb is to soak something up. The intestines absorb nutrients from food into the body.
Nutrients are the things in food, like vitamins and minerals, that help your body grow and work.
Bland means plain, with very little taste. The blandest dishes are the ones with the least flavour.

t: too much of a good thing
forms: too much of a good thing
text: This saying means something helpful turns bad when you have too much of it, like salt.
Taking a claim with a pinch of salt means not believing it right away. The writer plays on this saying because the article is about salt.
Proverbial means well known from a common saying. Here, the saying is to take something with a pinch of salt.
Fleur de sel is a fancy, expensive sea salt from France. Its name means flower of salt in French.
Himalayan means from the Himalayas, the huge mountain range in Asia. Pink Himalayan salt is mined there.
Sodium chloride is the scientific name for ordinary table salt.
Trace amounts are tiny bits, so small they are barely there.
Minerals are natural substances, like calcium, iron and zinc, that the body needs in small amounts.
A concentration is how much of a substance is packed into a certain amount of something else.
WHO stands for the World Health Organization, a group that gives health advice to countries around the world.
Additives are things added to food, such as iodine added to salt.
To be worth your salt means to be good at your job or truly useful. Here it is a joke: only two additives are truly useful.
Iodine is a mineral the body needs to grow a healthy brain and body. Iodised salt has it added.
Iodised salt is salt with iodine added to it. This is the British spelling.
Potassium is a mineral, a close cousin of sodium. Too little of it can push blood pressure up.
A physiologist is a scientist who studies how living bodies work.
A double whammy is two bad things happening at once. Too much sodium and too little potassium both raise blood pressure.
This saying means solving two problems with one action. Potassium salt cuts sodium and adds potassium at once.
Texture is how something feels, like smooth, crunchy or gritty.
An epidemiologist is a scientist who studies how diseases spread and what causes them in groups of people.
A stroke is when blood cannot reach part of the brain, which can cause serious harm. It is not the same as stroking a pet.
Rural means in the countryside, away from big towns and cities.
Standard means ordinary or usual. Standard table salt is the normal salt most people use.
Enriched means having something extra added. Here, the salt has potassium added.
Associated with means linked to. It says two things go together, though it does not prove one caused the other.
A simulation is a computer model that acts out what might happen in real life.
Here, to model means to use maths and a computer to predict what would happen. It is not a fashion model.
Complications are new problems that make an illness or situation harder.
Kidneys are two organs that clean waste out of your blood. People with kidney disease should be careful with potassium.
